title: NexaServe Human Content Approval Ledger
validation_rules: Only entries in the entries array are recorded decisions. example_entry_template is documentation and never a decision.
The entries array is empty at package creation; approved_record_count is zero.
A decision applies only to the exact source_dataset + source_record_id + content_hash_at_decision tuple.

Run scripts/validate_content_approval_ledger.py before use. It resolves every decision against source_approval_queue.json; a missing record or content-hash mismatch makes the decision STALE and blocks ledger acceptance.
Duplicate JSONL companions are parity artifacts, not distinct source_dataset values for approval or import.

An approved decision requires an evidence_reference and reviewer_role; official DEPI decisions require a verifiable official URL/document reference, and internal DEPI guidance requires an authorized content-owner decision.
No approval is inferred from a blank decision, missing evidence, workbook status, matching file hash, or absence of a response.
The source ledger decision enum is preserved. reviewer_identity is added to this proposed schema because the workbook captures it and it must not be lost during reconciliation.
Only explicit, complete, non-conflicting, current-hash decisions are written to entries. Incomplete or stale decisions remain only in the reconciliation report.

example_entry_template.source_dataset: <source JSON path from the approval queue>
example_entry_template.content_hash_at_decision: <64-character SHA-256 from the current approval queue>
example_entry_template.reviewer_role: <authorized reviewer role; do not use a placeholder in a real entry>
example_entry_template.timestamp_utc: <ISO-8601 UTC timestamp; do not use a placeholder in a real entry>
example_entry_template.notice: Illustrative template only. Not a source record, reviewer decision, approval, or supporting evidence.
